title: Apache Spark runtime in Fabric - Microsoft Fabric

claims.text: Fabric offers two Spark runtime generations: Runtime 1.3 is GA and carries Apache Spark 3.5.5, Delta Lake 3.2, Java 11, Scala 2.12.17, Python 3.11 on Mariner 2.0; Runtime 2.0 is Public Preview and carries Apache Spark 4.1, Delta Lake 4.2, Java 21, Scala 2.13.16, Python 3.13 on Mariner 3.0.
Microsoft's guidance is to run production workloads on the most recent GA runtime, currently Runtime 1.3, and all new workspaces default to the latest GA runtime rather than to the preview one.
The Native Execution Engine supports both Parquet and Delta formats across the Spark APIs on Runtime 1.3 (Spark 3.5) and Runtime 2.0 (Spark 4.1) — it is not a Runtime 2.0-only capability.

In Microsoft's representative TPC-DS benchmark at scale factor 1000 on Delta, the Native Execution Engine reached up to six times the performance of open-source Spark, which Microsoft translates to roughly 83% compute-cost savings on a fixed-size Fabric cluster.

Native execution is toggled per application with the spark.native.enabled configuration, and the Fabric Spark Advisor raises real-time alerts during notebook cell execution when a query falls back to JVM-based Spark.

Beyond open-source Spark, the Fabric Runtime adds close to a hundred built-in query performance enhancements (such as FileSystem partition caching to cut metastore calls) plus a built-in intelligent cache, all of which can be disabled to obtain standard Spark and Delta Lake behaviour.

Changing the runtime version migrates Spark settings automatically, but a setting incompatible with the target runtime is reported as a warning and not applied — so a silently missing setting after a runtime move is an expected, diagnosable outcome rather than a bug.

On a runtime change the library management system migrates public and custom libraries, and they keep working when the Python and R versions are unchanged; JARs have a significant chance of breaking because Scala, Java, Spark and the operating system all change, and resolving a conflicting library can fail the environment build outright.

Delta Lake features are backward compatible, but calling delta.upgradeTableProtocol raises the table's protocol version irreversibly and can leave existing readers or writers unable to access the table at all, so protocol upgrades gate interoperability with other Fabric engines.
